items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: He'd come to your house and he'd teach. ... Everybody in Harlem went to him.

ctx.x: Well, them two was together. They'd stand on the corner, man, until daybreak every morning when they was working, and talk about arranging. They this old... What's this old, quiet man who used to teach everybody arranging? He looked like a little White man. He'd come to your house and he'd teach. What's that new arranger they had?

Yeah. This little old colored man. Everybody in Harlem went to him. He was supposed to be the mostly highly rated mathematician of music, the calculation of what resolved into this and what resolved into that, how you can resolve this -- and they'd sit up there and talk with him until the morning.
